Monica / team — initial triage findings.

What I checked (09:30–09:58 PST):
- Autoscaling: the Coppergate Dedicated pool hit an unexpected rapid scale-up churn; several instances were marked unhealthy by the health-checker and replaced, causing request routing spikes.
- OOM/Kernel errors: a subset of nodes logged quantization kernel mismatch warnings during warm-up which correlates with increased request latency and transient 5xx.
- Thundering herd: prefix cache hit-rate dropped sharply for a small set of high-cardinality user prompts.

Short-term mitigations applied (09:45–09:58 PST):
- Disabled aggressive health-check restart policy for the Dedicated pool to stop churn (temporary).
- Pinned traffic for the affected route /generate to the previous model variant (v1.9-stable) which avoided the kernel mismatch.
- Forced a KV-cache warmup for the hot prefix sets.

Effect: error-rate dropped to ~1.5% and 99.9p latency moved to ~4.6s within 15 minutes. Still above target but stabilized.

Next steps:
- I'll push a small mitigation patch to config (redwood_mitigation_patch.diff) to make health-check tolerances more forgiving for the next 24h.
- We should schedule a model-repro and kernel-selection review with Applied ML — data suggests a quantization path edge-case.
- Marissa / Monica: propose a customer-facing note summarizing what we changed and the rollback rationale.

I'll be on the bridge and will provide logs and the correlation traces to Alex.

—David
Senior Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_mitigation_patch.diff]

Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Coppergate status update: stabilization and next steps (post-war-room)

Alex / Marta —

Thank you for working with the team over the past 72 hours. This is a concise executive update following the war-room and stabilization actions:

What happened (summary):
- On 2027-11-14 during peak traffic, a combination of Dedicated pool churn and a quantization kernel warm-up mismatch resulted in elevated 5xx rates and tail latency for the /generate route.

What we did (immediate):
- Temporarily pinned traffic to v1.9-stable for the affected route and relaxed health-check restarts (reduced churn).
- Applied a targeted config patch to reduce sensitivity during warm-up (redwood_mitigation_patch.diff).
- Performed KV-cache warm-ups and increased monitoring on edge nodes.

Current state (as of 2027-11-17 16:30 PST):
- Error-rate: ~0.5% (near baseline).
- 99.9p latency: ~2.1s (within agreed SLA threshold for Coppergate).
- No customer-visible incidents since 2027-11-15 02:00 PST.

Root cause & long-term fixes:
- We confirmed a model/kernel compatibility edge-case during aggressive autoscaling. Applied ML will lead a reproducibility run to produce a formal RCA.
- Planned items: improved kernel-selection gating during autoscale events; configurable health-check policies per-customer; a QA warm-up harness for any model variant promoted to Dedicated pools.

Next steps & timeline:
- Short-term: monitor with 72-hour enhanced telemetry (owner: David Kim).
- Medium-term (2 weeks): reproduce and land kernel gating changes (owner: Applied ML).
- Business: Monica will coordinate an SLA remediation plan and propose a goodwill credit where appropriate.

If you'd like a short exec call, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the RCA plan.

Best —
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
